S062.name: Specific_Phobic_Fear
S062.description: Marked fear or anxiety about a specific object or situation that is out of proportion to the actual danger. (Note: In children, may be expressed by crying, tantrums, freezing, or clinging).

subtypes.Animal Type: Marked fear of animals or insects like dogs, bees, snakes, or spiders.
subtypes.Natural Environment Type: Marked fear of the natural environment like storms, heights, water, or the dark.
subtypes.Blood-Injection-Injury Type: Marked fear of seeing blood, receiving injections, or medical procedures.
subtypes.Situational Type: Marked fear of specific situations like airplanes, elevators, tunnels, bridges, or enclosed spaces.
subtypes.Other Type: Marked fear of other situations like choking, vomiting, loud sounds, or costumed characters.

S063.name: Immediate_Fear/Anxiety_Response
S063.description: The phobic object or situation almost always provokes immediate fear or anxiety.

subtypes.Anticipatory Anxiety: Strong anxiety triggered just by thinking about the possibility of encountering the phobic object.
subtypes.Immediate Panic Response: Overwhelming fear erupting immediately upon facing the phobic object.
subtypes.Physiological Panic Symptoms: Intense physical reactions such as heart palpitations, shortness of breath, sweating, or trembling.
subtypes.Freezing: Feeling paralyzed or unable to move due to extreme fear.

S064.name: Phobic_Avoidance_Endure
S064.description: The phobic object or situation is actively avoided or endured with intense fear or anxiety.

subtypes.Active Avoidance: Intentionally and completely staying away from contact with the phobic object or situation.
subtypes.Functional Impairment due to Avoidance: Accepting severe restrictions on daily life, job, or social activities to avoid the phobic object.
subtypes.Enduring with Distress: Forcing oneself to endure the situation while experiencing intense fear and anxiety because it cannot be avoided.
subtypes.Reliance on Safety Signals: Barely enduring the exposure by relying on a companion or safety object.

symptom.disease_info: Specific Phobia is characterized by a persistent, excessive fear focused on a clearly identifiable object or situation (e.g., animals, heights, flying, blood/injury) that is out of proportion to the actual threat. The feared stimulus almost invariably elicits an immediate fear or anxiety response and is either avoided or endured with marked distress, typically lasting at least six months and causing significant interference in social, occupational, or other important areas of functioning. Unlike more generalized anxiety disorders, the fear in Specific Phobia is circumscribed rather than pervasive and is not better explained by other conditions such as OCD, PTSD, or social anxiety disorder. Onset often occurs in childhood but can emerge or re-emerge later in life after a triggering event or increased exposure, and many individuals present only when avoidance begins to conflict with key responsibilities or valued activities.

patient.stressor: Roughly thirteen months ago, Kayla slipped on an icy curb in her school’s parking lot and fractured her wrist, an incident that required a brief ER visit but no surgery. Although she healed physically and returned to teaching on schedule, the fall crystallized a long-standing but minor discomfort with hospitals and medical procedures into a much more pronounced dread of anything involving doctors’ offices, imaging suites, or invasive tests. Over the subsequent school year, as her chronic back issues began to flare from long hours at her desk and in the classroom, she repeatedly postponed recommended diagnostic appointments and physical therapy because planning those visits into her otherwise meticulously organized life became a source of escalating internal conflict and distress. When she ultimately canceled a long-awaited spine specialist consultation that she herself had pushed for, and her primary care physician warned her about the risks of continued delay and suggested that her avoidance might be anxiety-based, she reluctantly agreed to a mental health referral to understand why she was going to such lengths to stay away from medical settings.
patient.chief_complaint: I know it doesn’t make sense, but the thought of going into any kind of medical office or having tests done scares me so much that I keep putting off appointments I really need.

S062.name: Specific_Phobic_Fear
S062.description: Marked fear or anxiety about a specific object or situation that is out of proportion to the actual danger. (Note: In children, may be expressed by crying, tantrums, freezing, or clinging).
S062.manifestation: Ever since that fall and the trip to the ER, the idea of walking into any clinic or lying in one of those machines makes my stomach drop and my mind jump to worst‑case scenarios, even when I know logically it's probably just a routine test or a quick check‑up.

S063.name: Immediate_Fear/Anxiety_Response
S063.description: The phobic object or situation almost always provokes immediate fear or anxiety.
S063.manifestation: If I so much as get a reminder text from the doctor’s office or see a scene in a TV show where someone is getting an MRI, my heart starts pounding, my hands sweat, and I feel like I need to escape, even though I'm just sitting on my own couch.

S064.name: Phobic_Avoidance_Endure
S064.description: The phobic object or situation is actively avoided or endured with intense fear or anxiety.
S064.manifestation: I’ll spend weeks rearranging my schedule or coming up with excuses to cancel appointments, and on the rare occasions I force myself to go, I sit in the parking lot shaking, sometimes crying a little, and have to call my sister just to talk me through walking through the door.

add_requirements.functional_impairment: Because I keep canceling or delaying appointments, my back pain has gotten worse, I’ve missed several days of work when it flares, and my primary doctor has warned me I’m putting my health at risk by not following through on referrals.
add_requirements.duration: This intense fear around anything medical has been going on ever since my fall and ER visit about a year and a month ago.
